sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 WebGPURenderer, Rapier 3D 0.19.3, Web Audio API, Gamepad API, WebRTC, AI Hub Session Protocol v1; JavaScript in a single HTML
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded rooftop diorama with charcoal ink outlines, warm paper, teal water and orange accents
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip keyframe tracks for character idle and bomb toss; procedural particles and water movement
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated mallet music at 10% default volume, synthesized catches/splashes/explosions, formant-filtered Animalese-style gibberish; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 player shared-world co-op via AI Hub; standalone direct WebRTC invitation/reply; local two-player co-op
sourceInformation.testing: 205 automated checks across rules, audio, gamepad/touch UI, WebGPU drawing and device recovery, standalone WebRTC and the official AI Hub harness; full eight-wave scripted playthrough; GPU-readback screenshots. No physical controller, listener, TV or real mobile hardware available.
sourceInformation.research: Original Kaboom! manual and AtariAge game reference; source sound descriptions; official Three.js r180, Rapier and AI Hub documentation. Preserved stacked buckets, eight escalating groups, field-clearing misses, 1,000-point repairs and the taunting bomber; exact original audio synthesis parameters unknown.

testingFeedback: Testing and review caught 17 issues: three gameplay edge cases, one network rate-limit issue, eleven control/UI/integration issues, one graphics-device failure path, and one mouse-prompt mismatch. All were corrected. Final suite: 205 checks, zero failures.

One was potentially game breaking: a lost WebGPU device left the scene blank. Automatic recovery now replaces the canvas and restores rendering through WebGL 2. The supplied software-GPU flags caused the loss even in a one-cube test; corrected flags render WebGPU correctly.
The complete authoritative two-browser eight-wave playthrough was most helpful: it verified progression, independent controls, shared splash input, identical results and synchronized restart.
Fixed-duration input sleeps were least helpful on the software GPU. Replacing them with state-based waits removed test timing assumptions.
engineFeedback: Three.js makes procedural scene construction and native AnimationMixer clips straightforward. Rapier provides consistent fixed-step falling trajectories.
The supplied headless WebGPU flags destroyed even a one-cube device. Isolating the renderer, using working software-GPU flags and checking GPU texture readback resolved the uncertainty.
The arcade rules, controller-first focus navigation, procedural ink art/audio, authoritative networking and graphics recovery were built for this game.
Coordinating physics, native animation, asynchronous GPU initialization and host-authoritative snapshots while keeping controls consistent was hardest.
none; engine libraries are unmodified. The application adds device-loss recovery and uses the built-in WebGL 2 backend when needed.
A built-in cartoon outline pass with consistent WebGPU and WebGL behavior would simplify ink rendering.
promptFeedback: The recognizable source, complete vertical-slice requirement and controller-first direction gave the game a clear identity and a concrete finish line.
The standalone online lobby and signaling UX was unspecified. I selected direct WebRTC invitation/reply codes alongside automatic AI Hub sessions.
Delivering polished art, synthesized audio, touch assistance, attract play, developer tools and two multiplayer transports inside one portable HTML was hardest.
Specify whether standalone multiplayer should use a hosted room broker or direct invitation exchange, and distinguish mandatory features from optional polish.

aiHub.name: Ka-Splat!
aiHub.description: A rooftop rascal rains down trouble. Slide your three water buckets, unleash a splash shield, and conquer eight escalating waves alone or with a friend.
aiHub.controls: Move: left stick, D-pad, A/D, arrows or mouse; splash: Cross/A, Space or click; pause: Options/Menu or Esc; touch: drag and tap; P2: second pad or J/L and I.
